question: The region of Thessaly, and in particular the regional unit of Magnesia, has been pummelled in recent years by a series of extreme weather events and natural disasters, culminating in the widespread floods of September 2023 and the pollution of the Pagasetic Gulf in August 2024, both of which led to serious environmental and socio-economic consequences.

Local tourism businesses such as hotels, rooms for rent, the food service sector and outdoor activities businesses have suffered significant and prolonged loss of revenue, which has had a direct impact on the local economy.

In view of: - the Commission’s reply1 to my previous question2, in which it highlighted that it ‘is looking at various options to provide support to employees and businesses in Thessaly through comprehensive schemes which will allow them to adapt to change and strengthen their resilience in view of the ensuing challenges’; - the imminent adoption of the proposal to support Greece and four other European countries through the EU Solidarity Fund for the 2023 floods3, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What existing financial tools can be deployed quickly to support Thessaly’s tourism businesses and what are the possibilities of supporting these businesses through the transfer of funds from existing programmes?

Does it intend to look into the possibility of allowing for flexibility in the NSRF programmes or other financial tools in order to compensate tourism businesses for loss of revenue resulting from natural disasters?
Is it planning to look into the creation of a new financial tool to provide direct financial support to tourism businesses impacted by natural disasters?

Answer given my Ms Ferreira on behalf of the European Commission on 18 December 2023 https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-9-2023-003237-ASW_EN.html See the Commission proposal for the mobilisation of the European Union Solidarity Fund to provide assistance to Italy, Slovenia, Austria, Greece and France in support of recovery efforts following the serious flooding that took place in 2023. https://commission.europa.eu/publications/mobilisation-european-unionsolidarity-fund-2024_en?prefLang=el
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2024) As indicated in the reply provided to the written question E-003237/20231, in November 2023, Greece requested EU Solidarity Fund (EUSF) assistance for the storm ‘Daniel’ to cover part of the costs for emergency and recovery operations incurred by public authorities23. The Commission approved the application, paying an advance of EUR 25.

4 million in February 2024, with a balance of EUR 76.1 million due by year-end. Private damage is not eligible. Greece has not applied for EUSF assistance for the ecological catastrophe resulting in masses of dead fish appearing in the Pagasetic Gulf.

Greece’s Recovery and Resilience Plan4 supports the restoration of the damages to Thessaly’s road and railway network affected by storm ‘Daniel’ including the tourist train line of Pelion. For the 2021-2027 period, Greece benefits from the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) to promote business development and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)’ support including the Greek tourism ecosystem.

Indicatively, under the ‘Competitiveness’5 programme, a funding call aimed at strengthening the establishment and operation of new tourism SMEs has been launched, with a budget of EUR 160 million 6. However, compensation of businesses due to loss of revenues is not eligible for co-financing.
In accordance with ERDF Regulation7, the fund can support productive investments in SMEs and investments aiming at safeguarding existing jobs and creating new jobs.

In order to support resilient tourism, to help stakeholders to be better prepared, prevent and manage crisis, including natural disasters, the Commission under the Crisis management and governance in tourism project8, provided with digital learning models9, best practices and policy recommendations.
